title: How to Design a Wedding QR Code Card in Canva (Free, Step by Step)
description: Design your own wedding QR code card in Canva in 10 minutes — free, with step-by-step instructions and tips for a QR code that actually scans.
author: Guestcam Team
tldr: Open a free Canva design, add your names and date, drop in your Guestcam QR code image, and export a print-ready PDF — done in about 10 minutes.

content.text: Why design your own QR card

A generic printed QR code sign works, but a card you design yourself in Canva can match your wedding's colors, fonts, and overall look — so it feels like part of your decor instead of an afterthought taped to the table.
What you need before you start

items: Your Guestcam gallery's QR code, downloaded as a PNG (open your dashboard, go to the “QR koda” tab, and click “Prenesi samo QR kodo” — the Guestcam dashboard interface is in Slovenian, so those are the exact labels you'll see).
A free Canva account — no paid subscription required for this.

content.alt: Layout of a wedding QR code card: names and date at the top, QR code in the middle, a short instruction line below
content.caption: Keep it simple: names, QR code, one instruction line — that's all a card needs.

content.text: Step-by-step: designing the card in Canva

items: Go to canva.com and start a new design — search “postcard” or set a custom size of 10 × 15 cm (a good size for table cards).
Pick any template you like as a starting point, or start from a blank canvas.
Add a text box with your names, then a second one below with the wedding date.
Click Uploads → Upload files and add the QR code PNG you downloaded from your Guestcam dashboard.
Place the QR code in the center, sized at least 3 × 3 cm so phone cameras can focus on it easily.
Add one short instruction line underneath, e.g. “Scan & share your photos!”
Match the fonts and colors to your invitations for a cohesive look, then click Share → Download → PDF Print.

content.text: Design tips for a QR code that actually scans

items: Leave at least 8 mm of empty space (the “quiet zone”) around the QR code — phones use that margin to lock focus.
Don't shrink the code below roughly 3 × 3 cm on a table card, or 2 × 2 cm minimum on a badge.
Keep the QR code dark on a light background — low contrast is the most common reason a code fails to scan.
Never place the QR code over a busy photo or pattern.
Print one test card first and scan it yourself with two or three different phones before printing the full batch.

content.text: No time to design one? Use a ready-made template instead

If you'd rather skip the design work entirely, Guestcam includes 8 ready-made QR card templates that fill in your names and date automatically — download one as a print-ready PDF straight from your dashboard.

content.q: Do I need Canva Pro to make a QR code card?
content.a: No. A free Canva account covers everything in this guide — custom sizes, uploading your own QR code image, and PDF Print export.

content.q: Where do I get my wedding's QR code image?
content.a: From your Guestcam dashboard: open your gallery, go to the “QR koda” tab, and click “Prenesi samo QR kodo” to download it as a PNG.

content.q: What size should I print the card?
content.a: A6 (roughly 10.5 × 14.8 cm) works well for table cards. Use A5 or A4 for a larger sign near the entrance or gift table.

content.q: Why didn't my printed QR code scan?
content.a: The most common causes are a low-resolution image (always use the downloaded file, never a screenshot), too little white space around the code, or a code printed too small. Test-scan before printing the full batch.
